title: Moldova tops the medal table at the Balkan Senior Championships
excerpt: In Sarajevo, the Republic of Moldova finished first in the medal table of the Balkan Senior Championships, with 10 medals: 8 gold, 1 silver and 1 bronze.
body_html:
Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, is where the Republic of Moldova finished first in the overall medal table of the Balkan Senior Table Tennis Championships, with an unprecedented total of 10 medals: 8 gold, 1 silver and 1 bronze.

The Moldovan delegation's performance was capped by a historic individual result. Vladislav URSU became the overall men's champion, winning gold in every event he played. No player had ever done this before in the men's events in the history of the Balkan Senior Championships, which makes the result in Sarajevo a first for the competition.

It is the best result ever achieved by a Moldovan delegation at this competition and one of the few times in the tournament's history that a single country has collected so many medals.

The result in Sarajevo is not an isolated one. This year, Moldova's representatives won a bronze medal at the European Championships, and at the World Championships in London the national team qualified for the final stage of the competition.

This run of results points to a sustained development of Moldovan table tennis over the past year.

Over the past year, the associate members of the Table Tennis Federation of the Republic of Moldova have made a series of structural changes and changes of approach in preparing the national squads, and the results achieved in 2026 are a concrete indicator of the effect of these measures and of the direction in which the sport is now developing nationally.
